1️⃣ Normal Distribution (Gaussian Curve)
In a normal distribution:
●​ Mean = Median = Mode​
●​ The curve is symmetric​
●​ Most values cluster around the center​
👉 This equality is a key indicator of normality.
2️⃣ Measures of Central Tendency
🔹 Mean
●​ Arithmetic average​
●​ Sum of all observations ÷ number of observations​
🔹 Median
●​ Middle value after sorting data from smallest to largest​
🔹 Mode
●​ Most frequent value​
●​ Appears at the peak of the Gaussian curve​

Modiﬁable risk factors
Smoking: Smoking plays a role in the buildup of plaque on the
inner lining of the arteries, decreased oxygen supply to the blood,
elevated blood pressure and increased risk of heart disease.
Physical inactivity: A low level of physical activity is associated
with a high risk of heart disease and death. Try to schedule at least
150 minutes per week of moderate-to-vigorous intensity physical
activity. If you are a person with heart disease or are starting an
exercise program, discuss this with your doctor first.
Poor nutrition: a high intake of saturated fats combined with a
low intake of fruits and vegetables increases the risk of
cardiovascular disease.

health risk factors.

Risk and Protective Factors
Protective factors are attributes, like skills, strengths or
resources, that help shield individuals from the development or
worsening of undesirable health conditions and enhance their
capacity to cope.
Risk factors are attributes that contribute to the development
or worsening of undesirable conditions. For example, risk
factors include oppositional behaviours, familial conflict and
social isolation. Any of those might increase the risk of mood
disorders or maladaptive behaviours such as drug and alcohol
consumption.

body.text:
What Is the Rationale for Health Indicators?
Indicators are vital in health interventions because, when collected and used
regularly, they can:
• allow us to monitor health status of populations (who is dying, from what, who
is ill, etc.).
• provide evidence for public-health planning and resource allocation (if we know
a region has a high infant-mortality rate, then we can target interventions).
• help to evaluate policies and programmes (did the intervention reduce disease
incidence? did the healthcare coverage improve?).
• permit comparison across time and place (so we know if things are improving or
worsening, and how one country/region compares to another).
